questions.question: Which placeholder tokens should the prefix template support? (repo nickname is always the base; pick the others to wire up now)

options.label: {host} — mini/note
options.description: Host nickname, only filled for host-local bridge sessions (cloud sessions leave it empty). This is what you asked for first.

options.label: {branch} — git branch
options.description: The worktree's git branch. Local bridge sessions only, and costs one git call per session during the monitor's self-heal pass.

options.label: {repo} — full repo name
options.description: The full repo basename (e.g. FamilyFund) as an alternative token to the {nick} nickname (FF).

options.label: {engine} — claude/codex
options.description: The agent engine. Note: titled code-sessions are effectively always claude, so this is usually constant.

questions.question: Where should the template string be configured, and what default?

options.label: Env + nicknames file (Recommended)
options.description: SESSION_TITLE_FORMAT env var, overridable by a `format=...` header line in session-nicknames.txt. Default template: {repo}.{host}. Matches the existing nickname-config pattern.

options.label: Env var only
options.description: Just SESSION_TITLE_FORMAT, default {repo}.{host}. Simplest; no file changes.

options.label: New dedicated config file
options.description: A separate session-title-format.txt file at the repo root.

questions.question: When a token has no value (e.g. {host} on a cloud session), how should the template render?

options.label: Collapse token + separator (Recommended)
options.description: {repo}.{host} renders as `FF` (the empty {host} and its leading `.` are dropped); on a bridge session it's `FF.mini`. Keeps titles clean.

options.label: Leave blank
options.description: {repo}.{host} renders as `FF.` on a cloud session (trailing separator kept). Simpler rule, uglier output.
